incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (中華民國公司法), Articles 1, 98-101, 128-131, 161, 208, 277, 387; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 6, 8; Enterprise Registration Act (商業登記法), Articles 5-7.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, R.O.C.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Company Registration Application Form (公司設立登記申請書)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital for general service industry; however foreign investment funds must be remitted into a designated foreign-currency account in Taiwan and certified by a bank as paid-up capital before filing; paid-in capital may be lower than authorized capital at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The subscribers of this Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, having completed capital remittance and escrow certification, be and are hereby allotted the initial paid-in shares; (2) the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [Address], Taiwan, R.O.C., and the Articles of Incorporation as filed with the Department of Commerce are ratified; (3) [Name] be and is hereby elected as Chairperson/Representative Director; (4) [Name] be and is hereby appointed as General Manager and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, with authority to open bank accounts and execute statutory filings; (5) the seal and corporate chop of the Company are adopted for use in commercial transactions and regulatory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER that all actions already taken to effect incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign Investment Application Form (FIA-1) online through the MOEA Investment Commission portal. Submit scanned originals, including investor passport or juridical person certificate, power of attorney, and business scope description. The Commission reviews for negative-list restrictions and issues an investment approval letter. No notarization is required for this step, but documents in foreign languages must be translated into Chinese and certified.
required_dossiers: Audited financial statements (if investor is a juridical person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit supplementary explanation within 30 days via the portal; if denied, file an administrative appeal (訴願) with MOEA within 30 days after receiving the denial notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for company name pre-approval and business scope alignment through the Company Registration Information System. Ensure the Chinese name includes a designation for 'Limited Company' (有限公司). The system performs name-conflict search against registered companies. The reservation lasts for six months and can be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Pre-approval of foreign investment letter (if already issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name reservation is rejected due to similarity, file a new application with a modified name or submit a letter of consent from the conflicting registrant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance and Paid-Up Capital Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank (selected by the Company) and Central Bank of China, R.O.C.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a foreign-currency deposit account and remit the contributed capital from shareholders. The bank will issue a foreign exchange certificate and a capital remittance certification. The funds must remain deposited and not be withdrawn until the company registration is completed. The certification document is required for the incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If remittance is blocked, provide additional source-of-funds evidence or obtain bank approval for a refund; if certification is defective, obtain a corrected bank statement and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Shareholder Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office (civil-law notarization optional) and founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a founding shareholders' meeting to adopt the Articles of Incorporation, elect directors and the chairperson, and appoint the manager. Shareholders must sign the articles; if a shareholder is a foreign company, the signature or seal of its legal representative must be certified either by a Taiwan notary or by the Taiwan overseas mission. The minutes of the founding meeting must record capital subscription and appointment of officers.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the founding shareholders' meeting
Certificate of incorporation of foreign shareholder (if applicable)
Power of attorney for physical person signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is queried, cure by providing corrected signatures or a re-executed power of attorney; all documents that fail authentication must be replaced and re-notarized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Filing with Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA (one-stop counter, including local business registration and filiations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Company Registration Application together with all notarized/authenticated documents through the One-Stop Company Registration Portal or in person at the MOEA Department of Commerce. Pay the filing fee and the certificate fee. The Department reviews compliance with the Company Act and registers the company. Upon approval, the company receives the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書).
required_dossiers: Minutes of founding shareholders' meeting and board meeting
Power of attorney and ID copies of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the deficiency notice within 15 days; if amendments are required, refile the corrected documents online. For registration denial, an administrative appeal may be filed within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Corporate Seal Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau and local business administration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for tax identification number (TIN, 統編), invoice (uniform invoice) registration, and corporate seal (company chop) recordation. The TIN registration can be done online or at the local tax bureau. Obtain a corporate seal and record the specimen with the Department of Commerce and tax bureau. This step completes the basic corporate governance foundation and authorizes the company to commence limited post-formation activities such as opening bank accounts and signing contracts.
required_dossiers: Local operating site address proof (lease or ownership document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed or queried, provide the tax office with modified details and re-submit the application; if the address proof is defective, provide a supplementary lease certificate and landlord ID.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Testing Laboratory Registration / Designated Testing Laboratory Accreditation for UN38.3 Battery Safety Testing (電芯及電池組安全試驗實驗室) — issued under the Commodity Inspection Act and ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation by TAF (Taiwan Accreditation Foundation)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan (EPD / 環境部)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D5 — Registration/exemption from full EIA assessment; subject to Environmental Pollution Prevention Facility Approval and Toxic Chemical Substances Registration for small-scale laboratory operations (if using designated chemicals, apply for a Toxic Chemical Substance Permit).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must meet effluent standards under the Water Pollution Control Act (pH 6-9, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, SS ≤ 30 mg/L); volatile organic solvent emissions from lab operations must be controlled under the Air Pollution Control Act; waste lithium batteries and battery samples must be declared as general/managed industrial waste and delivered to a licensed hazardous waste contractor for recycling or disposal; empty solvent drums must be cleared via manifest tracking.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification from the local Fire Bureau (fire extinguishers, alarm system, and emergency lighting); Building Structural Load Inspection certificate from a licensed structural engineer for the laboratory area; Occupational Safety Clearance (occupational injury and health risk assessment) from the Ministry of Labor, including electrical safety, high-voltage battery testing containment, and personnel protective equipment compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (国家税务总局, STA), operating through the National Unified E-Tax Bureau portal (全国统一规范电子税务局, etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and the 12366 tax service hotline. The Shenzhen/Shanghai or local STA branch where the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture laboratory is registered exercises day-to-day administration. All filings, VAT general taxpayer qualification, and e-invoice quotas are managed electronically under the Golden Tax Phase IV (金税四期) system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must complete company incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which simultaneously assigns the 18-character Unified Social Credit Code (统一社会信用代码) that functions as the statutory TIN/VAT registration number. Within 30 days of obtaining the business license, the JV completes tax registration (税务登记) via the E-Tax Bureau portal by filing: (1) the SAMR business license; (2) the Foreign Investment Filing Certificate (外商投资信息报告); (3) the Articles of Association and Joint Venture Contract; (4) registered address proof and lease agreement; and (5) legal representative and finance officer identification. Upon completion, STA issues the Taxpayer Qualification Information, activates the VAT taxpayer classification (General or Small-Scale), enables the UKey digital certificate, sets the invoice quota, and binds the enterprise bank account to the Golden Tax system for real-time reconciliation. No separate TIN is required for a domestically incorporated EJV; the JV is a Chinese resident taxpayer in its own right.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not maintain a check-the-box or pass-through regime; all equity joint ventures are classified as C corporation equivalents taxed at entity level under Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) at a 25% headline rate on worldwide income. Available statutory elections relevant to the laboratory: (i) VAT classification election between Small-Scale Taxpayer (simplified 3% levy, subject to annual turnover ≤ RMB 5 million and full compliance) and General Taxpayer (input credit mechanism at 6% for modern technical services); (ii) EIT collection-method election between audit-based assessment (查账征收, the default and mandatory benchmark) and the restricted deemed-assessment method (核定征收); (iii) the 100% super-deduction election for qualifying R&D expenditures (研发费用加计扣除, applicable to laboratory test-method development); (iv) accelerated depreciation / one-time expensing election for research and testing equipment under current accelerated-depreciation rules; (v) the 15% reduced EIT rate election available only where the JV qualifies as an encouraged industry enterprise or an advanced-technology service enterprise within the designated pilot zones; and (vi) the foreign-tax-credit election on notional cross-border service income. Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable; anti-deferral and transfer-pricing rules apply to cross-border service payments to the Taiwan parent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope_note: As a Chinese resident enterprise, the JV is subject to EIT on its worldwide income; foreign-source income (e.g., fees earned from wholly offshore testing engagements) is taxable in China with a foreign tax credit, while the Taiwan parent jurisdiction applies its own territorial regime on repatriated dividends.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.national_tax_registration_infrastructure: The laboratory requires a separate VAT registration in the local STA branch where its testing facility is physically located; branch or cross-province laboratory locations require separate registrations for VAT and local surcharges (urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, and local education surcharge at combined rates of 7%, 3% and 2% of the VAT paid).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax, 增值税) under the PRC VAT Law of 2024 and its implementing regulations; the EJV laboratory renders taxable modern-service output classified under technical services (技术类现代服务) at the standard 6% service rate, with the general 13% rate reserved for goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory General VAT taxpayer registration. A small-scale taxpayer with annual sales not exceeding RMB 5,000,000 may elect simplified taxation at 3% (temporarily reduced to 1% during the relief window); monthly sales not exceeding RMB 100,000 (or quarterly RMB 300,000) are wholly VAT-exempt for small-scale taxpayers. Because the JV performs high-value UN38.3 testing contracts and must issue full credit-bearing invoices to corporate clients, it is registered as a General VAT taxpayer at 6% on testing, certification, and electromagnetic compliance fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory fully digitalized electronic invoices (全面数字化电子发票, 数电票) are issued through the STA centralized E-Tax Bureau platform under Golden Tax Phase IV; physical paper invoices are phased out. Every invoice is assigned a digitized serial number in real time and cleared against the STA big-data cloud before issuance; the UKey-based identity authentication is compulsory. Invoice amounts, VAT payable, and declared sales are automatically cross-reconciled with bank settlement data, corporate income tax returns, and the foreign-exchange payment records held by banks. Cross-border service fee remittances require the Service Trade and Other Items Foreign Exchange Payment Tax Record Form (服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表) to be filed with STA prior to the bank effecting remittance to the Taiwan parent or overseas recipient. Failure to issue a compliant 数电票 or any mismatch between invoice data and bank inflows triggers immediate system alert, taxpayer image downgrade, and invoice-quota suspension.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.special_indirect_tax_nexus_rules: Physical battery samples imported from Taiwan into the JV laboratory for UN38.3 destructive testing are temporarily imported in bond; the import VAT and customs duty on such samples are not creditable against output VAT and must be either bonded-exempt (if re-exported after testing, notwithstanding destructive consumption) or expensed. The laboratory's local technical-service output is wholly within the PRC place-of-supply rules because the testing activity occurs inside China; an overseas principal does not shift the supply location offshore merely because the report is delivered abroad.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Battery UN38.3 drop and electromagnetic testing is NOT eligible for export zero-rating under the 财税〔2016〕36号 Annex 4 positive list. The zero-rate categories are limited to international transport, offshore R&D, design, software, information-systems, consultancy (certain classes), and integrated-circuit design and testing services 'completely consumed outside China.' Physical battery-safety drop testing executed within a PRC laboratory is a domestic place-of-supply service consumed at the location of the testing bench; the STA negative-list position treats such testing as fully domestically consumed and therefore taxable at 6%, even where the contracting principal is the Taiwan parent, all fees are paid in foreign exchange, and the technical report is transmitted offshore. Zero-rating (0%) or exemption (免税) would be available only in the exceptional structure where the goods being tested are never brought into China and the JV's engineers perform the test protocols at an overseas facility or remotely on samples located abroad; in that case the complete-consumption test is satisfied, the Cross-Border Service Exemption/Zero-Rating Filing is admitted, and input VAT on the related service costs becomes refundable or creditable under the general-taxpayer mechanism. For the standard import-to-China sample flow, no refund path exists and the 6% VAT is the final cost.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration for re-exported battery samples after destructive testing (or bonded warehouse exit declaration)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill proving physical cross-strait movement of samples to and from Taiwan
Inward Remittance Certificate (境外汇款申请书暨涉外收入申报单) issued by the settlement bank evidencing receipt of testing fees from Taiwan within the repatriation deadline
Signed UN38.3 testing Service Agreement identifying the offshore principal and the testing scope
Service Trade and Other Items Foreign Exchange Payment Tax Record Form (服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表)
Final test reports and data transmittal logs proving offshore delivery of the testing outcome
Commercial invoice, packing list, and dangerous-goods air transport declaration for the imported battery samples
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA integrates Golden Tax invoice data, Customs trade data, and bank foreign-exchange receipts; any testing-services zero-rating or exemption claim is audited against the physical location of the test equipment, the customs entry records of the battery samples, and the 180-day FX repatriation trail. Where zero-rating/exemption is successfully claimed and later found ineligible: the full VAT output tax becomes immediately payable (retroactive to the invoice issuance date), daily late-payment surcharges accrue at 0.05% per day, and the administrative penalty ranges from 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid pursuant to the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection (Article 63) and the VAT Law implementing rules. The JV is additionally exposed to: (i) loss of the audit-based collection mode with forced deemed-profit taxation; (ii) freeze and reduction of its 数电票 invoice quota; (iii) inclusion in the serious-tax-violation taxpayer blacklist with joint disciplinary sanctions on its legal representative; (iv) clawback of any VAT refunds plus interest in the currency of the refund; and (v) criminal liability for fraudulent export-tax-refund or false-invoice offenses (虚开增值税专用发票, tax fraud) where the misrepresentation is deliberate, carrying penalties up to life imprisonment and fines in addition to the tax clawback.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.transfer_pricing_cross_border_context: The testing fee charged to the Taiwan parent must be at arm's length; the STA applies the OECD-aligned transfer-pricing rules and the cross-border service conduit rules. A fee below cost or a royalty-free zero-margin arrangement triggers a transfer-pricing adjustment that re-characterizes the income as taxable at 25% EIT plus surcharge, and the denied tax-deduction is imposed as a deemed dividend to the Taiwan parent subject to 10% dividend withholding tax under the Cross-Strait agreement or domestic law. The 6% VAT, where not zero-rated, is borne by the foreign principal unless the contract shifts it to the JV with gross-up.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Dual-jurisdiction control: (i) for the PRC parent JV, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the People's Republic of China (国家外汇管理局, SAFE) governs capital-account convertibility, outward direct investment registration and cross-border trade verification; (ii) for the Taiwan operating entity, the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (中央銀行, CBC) is the monetary and foreign-exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (管理外匯條例) and supervises all designated foreign-exchange banks (指定外匯銀行, DBU). The Financial Supervisory Commission (金融監督管理委員會, FSC) supplements bank licensing and AML/CFT enforcement in Taiwan.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan maintains a de facto fully convertible current account: receipts and payments for testing services may be freely converted through a DBU after the filing of a CBC foreign-exchange declaration (外匯收支或交易申報書) for each transaction with a TWD equivalent of NT$500,000 or more. The capital account is selectively restricted: a mainland Chinese investor must obtain prior approval from the MOEA Investment Commission (投審會) under the 大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法, after which the remitted equity capital can be converted at market rates without separate CBC conversion approval. Profit and dividend repatriation to the PRC parent is permissible after audited financial statements and a valid dividend resolution, subject to withholding tax settlement, the CBC declaration, and confirmation that no unfulfilled investment conditions remain. A practical structural hurdle is the absence of a deep direct interbank TWD/CNY market; settlement is typically triangulated through USD, or through the cross-strait RMB clearing arrangement operated by Bank of China Taipei Branch (中國銀行臺北分行), which prices TWD/RMB on a deliverable basis.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: PRC side (parent JV): export proceeds must be repatriated to China (調回境內) within the trade-receipt verification window normally set at 90 days from customs clearance, with deferred-receipt registration extending the window to 180 days and advance receipts arriving 30+ days before shipment requiring registration in the SAFE trade monitoring system; no mandatory conversion applies, so the JV may retain 100% of receipts in its foreign-currency settlement account or convert into CNY at its discretion. Taiwan side (operating subsidiary): under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act and CBC implementing rules, the subsidiary must negotiate service export proceeds by either selling the foreign exchange to a DBU or placing it into a foreign-currency deposit account at a DBU within 180 days from completion of the testing service (invoice date for services); retention beyond 180 days requires a documented application to the CBC. Because laboratory billings are predominantly EUR- and USD-denominated from EU battery and electronics manufacturers, treasury should accumulate balances in the DBU foreign-currency account and execute periodic EUR/USD to TWD spot conversions aligned with payroll and opex cycles.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approval and Filing with Shareholder Meeting Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Central Commercial Registration Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ends December 31; shareholder meeting approving annual financial statements must occur by June 30; filing with MOEA within 15 days of approval (by July 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of NT$10,000–50,000 per month for late filing; repeated non-compliance may trigger an MOEA order for dissolution and administrative strike-off of company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Report Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return must be filed by May 31 of the following calendar year; payment of assessed tax due on the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest is charged monthly; late filing penalty of 10% of assessed tax (up to NT$30,000) plus an additional 1% penalty every 30 days of delay; non-filing ultimately enables tax authority to estimate assessment and enforce collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 or on the date prescribed in the foreign investment approval letter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may impair the foreign investor's right to legally repatriate dividends and profits, trigger administrative fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, and adversely affect future investment approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Meeting and Minutes Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Central Commercial Registration Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Regular shareholders' meeting must be convened within six months of fiscal year-end (by June 30); minutes must be filed with MOEA within 15 days of the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance subject to NT$10,000–50,000 administrative penalty; continuous failure to convene or file may lead to judicial compulsory dissolution at public prosecutor's or interested party's request.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent CPA audit is required when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 1 million), when the company has publicly issued securities, or when MOEA or relevant regulations require certification; smaller unlisted joint ventures may be exempt unless the shareholders' agreement or foreign parent consolidation policy requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Republic of China GAAP (Business Entity Accounting Standards) applies to unlisted private companies; Taiwan-IFRS is mandatory for listed companies and financial institutions; a Sino-foreign joint venture may prepare an additional IFRS package to satisfy foreign parent reporting requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a standalone annual UBO return for a private unlisted joint venture. Annual confirmation of the registered shareholding structure is performed at the ordinary shareholders' meeting, where the register of members is reviewed. Every share transfer must be recorded in the share transfer register and filed with MOEA within 15 days of the transfer. Foreign shareholders must report changes in ownership to the Investment Commission through the approved foreign investment record and the annual foreign investment operations report.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D expenditure tax credits (15% of qualifying spending), investment tax credits for smart machinery, 5G equipment, energy-efficient installations, and limited tax exemptions for eligible start-up enterprises, all subject to statutory caps and recapture conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Form 1, 營利事業所得稅結算申報書), filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance e-Filing Portal (https://tax.nat.gov.tw/).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement; interim provisional tax payment on first-half-year income is due within 30 days after the half-year close.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the end of the taxable year; calendar-year entities file by 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from battery safety testing, electromagnetic compatibility assessments, and other accredited laboratory services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue is recorded in Taiwan books; non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation for this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct production costs including testing consumables, equipment depreciation, calibration charges, and certified labor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses actually incurred and documented in Taiwan are accepted; charges paid to foreign related laboratories must pass arm's-length benchmarking.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Automatically computed gross profit derived from Box 01 minus Box 02.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If cross-border controlled transactions exist, a transfer-pricing adjustment may be reflected in this figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses, including rent, salaries, utilities, professional fees, and office costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Taiwan-related expenditures are deductible; allocations from a foreign head office require contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit prior to applying statutory incentives and prior-year loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed solely at the Taiwan entity level; non-resident shareholders do not compute this for the JV.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax at 20% after applying exemptions, credits, and carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The JV self-assesses and pays; foreign shareholders receive dividends subject to separate withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 1% of the assessed tax (maximum 12% of the tax amount), plus interest; failure to file after an official reminder leads to an estimated assessment and an additional penalty up to 3 times the tax under Article 108 of the Income Tax Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to a non-Taiwanese resident enterprise without a Taiwan fixed place of business.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For treaty jurisdictions, the corporate shareholder must submit a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) and a completed treaty relief application to the local tax authority before payment; the payer then withholds at the reduced treaty rate or applies for a refund when tax has been over-withheld. The Cross-Strait Tax Agreement with mainland China has been signed but is not yet in force, so statutory withholding currently applies to PRC shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 20%, interest 20% on gross amounts; under effective DTAs, rates may be reduced (usually to 10% for both royalties and interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File (transfer pricing report) is required when annual controlled transactions exceed NT$50 million; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds NT$30 billion; Country-by-Country Report obligations attach at approximately NT$27 billion of group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies a general anti-avoidance rule (Article 12-1 of the Tax Evasion and Penalty Act) and Article 43-1 transfer-pricing recharacterization powers. Although no formal circular-style ESR statute exists, the testing laboratory must maintain a real and substantive presence: physical premises, qualified staff, testing equipment, actual operational decisions in Taiwan, and credible documentation of testing activities. Artificial booking of profits without such substance may lead to recharacterization and penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting testing revenue, fabricating expense invoices, maintaining double books, or intentionally submitting false financial statements to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Evasion and Penalty Act: imprisonment up to 5 years, detention, or a fine up to NT$6 million; together with reassessment, delayed-payment interest, and a monthly surcharge of 1% up to 12%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general managers, and accounting officers who knowingly organize or consent to the fraud may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and imposed fines; a travel ban may be requested under Article 24; for intentional concealment, courts may pierce the corporate veil for civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording profits in the Taiwan entity without real operational substance, such as no functioning laboratory, no qualified staff, no equipment, or routing testing through offshore subcontractors solely to exploit tax rate differentials.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization under Article 12-1 and TP adjustment under Article 43-1; the tax authority may reallocate income to the true economic owner, impose additional tax at 20%, add late-interest, and levy administrative fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the entity to operate as a shell may be personally assessed for constructive dividends; the corporate veil may be pierced for unpaid tax liabilities where the company is found to be a sham, and officers can face imprisonment for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments above NT$500,000 without filing a Cash Transaction Report (CTR), failing to perform customer identification, or neglecting beneficial-owner verification for corporate clients in the testing business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, administrative fines up to NT$10,000,000, possible suspension or revocation of the laboratory accreditation, and FIU asset-freeze orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers who knowingly fail to report or intentionally conceal suspicious transactions face criminal imprisonment (up to 2 years under the regulatory reporting provisions and up to 7 years for active acts of money laundering), personal criminal fines, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Neglect on Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, royalties, or interest to a foreign parent, shareholder, or IP licensor without deducting and paying the mandatory Taiwanese withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is held liable for the un-withheld tax amount plus late-payment interest and administrative penalties; penalties may range from 10% to 30% of the unpaid sum, with a maximum fine of NT$1,000,000 in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who approve such payments without adequate due diligence may be personally liable for the withheld tax and penalties; in cases of fraudulent avoidance, criminal liability under the Tax Evasion and Penalty Act may extend to imprisonment.
